title: Coal & Lignite Fields
blurb: Gondwana coal basins and tertiary lignite deposits across India.

places.name: Jharia
places.fact: India's sole storehouse of prime coking coal; famous for chronic underground mine fires in the Damodar Valley.

places.name: Bokaro
places.fact: Vital medium-coking coal source feeding Bokaro and Rourkela steel plants in Damodar Valley.

places.name: Raniganj
places.fact: India's oldest commercial coalfield opened in 1774; non-coking coal with high volatile matter.

places.name: Talcher
places.fact: Massive thermal non-coking coal reserve along the Brahmani river valley supporting NTPC plants.

places.name: Korba
places.fact: Key Hasdeo river basin field powering the Korba super thermal power station and BALCO.

places.name: Singrauli
places.fact: Son river valley field known as India's Energy Capital; thickest coal seam in India (Purewa).

places.name: Neyveli
places.fact: Largest open-cast brown coal / lignite deposit in India operated by NLC India in Cuddalore district.

places.name: Palana
places.fact: Tertiary lignite basin in Bikaner district utilized for thermal power generation.

places.name: North Karanpura
places.fact: Major coalfield in Upper Damodar basin with extensive pithead power generation.

places.name: Kothagudem
places.fact: Anchor field of Singareni Collieries (SCCL) in the Pranhita-Godavari valley.

places.name: Chandrapur
places.fact: Wardha valley coalfield sustaining Western Coalfields Ltd (WCL) thermal supply.

places.name: Ib Valley
places.fact: Part of the Mahanadi basin coalfields with extensive open-cast power-grade coal extraction.

places.name: Makum
places.fact: Tertiary coalfield in upper Assam known for high-sulphur, low-ash metallurgical coal.

places.name: Nichahom
places.fact: Karewa formation lignite deposit located in Kupwara district of Kashmir valley.

places.name: Giridih
places.fact: High-grade metallurgical coal repository, home to the historic Karharbari seam.

places.name: Sohagpur
places.fact: Major coal belt in Son valley basin operated by South Eastern Coalfields Limited.

questions.question: Which river valley hosts the prominent coalfields of Jharia, Bokaro and Raniganj?
questions.explanation: The Damodar Valley is renowned as the Ruhr of India and holds India's richest Gondwana coal deposits.

questions.question: Which type of coal has the highest carbon content and lowest moisture?
questions.explanation: Anthracite has >85% carbon content; found in small quantities in Jammu & Kashmir (Reasi).

questions.question: Which Indian state holds the largest reserves of Lignite (brown coal)?
questions.explanation: Tamil Nadu accounts for over 80% of India's identified lignite resources, centered around Neyveli.

questions.question: The Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL) operates primarily in which river basin?
questions.explanation: SCCL operates in the Godavari Valley coalfield in Telangana.

title: Oil & Gas Fields
blurb: Major onshore basins and continental shelf offshore hydrocarbon reserves.

places.name: Digboi
places.fact: Oldest continuously operating oilfield and refinery in Asia, discovered in 1889.

places.name: Naharkatiya
places.fact: First post-independence oil discovery in India (1953) along Burhi Dihing river.

places.name: Bombay High
places.fact: India's most prolific offshore oilfield on the continental shelf discovered in 1974, operated with Sagar Samrat.

places.name: Bassein
places.fact: Giant offshore natural gas field located south of Bombay High in the Arabian Sea.

places.name: Ankleshwar
places.fact: Pivotal onshore Cambay basin discovery described by Jawaharlal Nehru as the 'Fountain of Prosperity'.

places.name: Kalol
places.fact: Major North Cambay basin field producing heavy paraffinic crude oil near Ahmedabad.

places.name: Mehsana
places.fact: Prolific heavy-oil producing onshore asset of ONGC with cyclic steam stimulation.

places.name: Mangala (Barmer)
places.fact: Largest onshore oil discovery in India in over two decades, located in Thar desert (Cairn).

places.name: Ravva Field
places.fact: Key offshore oil and natural gas production asset in the Krishna-Godavari (KG) shallow offshore.

places.name: Moran-Hugrijan
places.fact: Upper Assam basin oilfield feeding the Barauni and Bongaigaon pipeline grid.

places.name: Cambay (Lunej)
places.fact: First oil discovery by ONGC in Gujarat (1958) validating structural traps in Tertiary sediments.

places.name: Narimanam
places.fact: Important hydrocarbon producing onshore field in the Cauvery sedimentary basin.

questions.question: The 'Sagar Samrat' drillship is historically associated with which iconic offshore field?
questions.explanation: Sagar Samrat drilled the discovery well in Bombay High in February 1974.

questions.question: Where was the first commercially successful oil well drilled in India?
questions.explanation: The first oil well was drilled in Digboi in 1889, leading to Asia's first oil refinery.

questions.question: Which sedimentary basin hosts the deepwater gas fields of KG-D6?
questions.explanation: KG-D6 is located in the Krishna-Godavari deepwater basin off the coast of Andhra Pradesh.

title: Oil Refineries
blurb: Coastal and inland petroleum refining centers of strategic importance.

places.name: Jamnagar
places.fact: World's largest grassroots refining complex owned by Reliance Industries (export-oriented).

places.name: Vadinar
places.fact: Second-largest single-site refinery in India operated by Nayara Energy in Gulf of Kutch.

places.name: Digboi
places.fact: Asia's oldest operating oil refinery commissioned in 1901 by Assam Oil Company.

places.name: Barauni
places.fact: Constructed with Soviet and Romanian assistance in 1964; fed by pipeline from Assam and Paradip.

places.name: Mathura
places.fact: Inland refinery equipped with sulfur scrubbers to protect the marble of the Taj Mahal.

places.name: Haldia
places.fact: Port-based coastal refinery producing specialized lubricating base oils and fuels.

places.name: Paradip
places.fact: Modern deep-conversion coastal refinery of Indian Oil with an integrated polypropylene unit.

places.name: Visakhapatnam
places.fact: East coast refinery of HPCL handling imported high-sulfur crude crudes.

places.name: Kochi
places.fact: Largest public sector refinery in India (BPCL) situated near the Vembanad backwaters.

places.name: Mangalore
places.fact: MRPL coastal refinery situated near New Mangalore Port with single point mooring.

places.name: Bina
places.fact: Originally built as a JV with Oman Oil (BORL), now fully integrated with BPCL.

places.name: Guru Gobind Singh (Bhatinda)
places.fact: HPCL-Mittal Energy Limited (HMEL) inland refinery linked to Mundra port via crude pipeline.

places.name: Panipat
places.fact: Major north Indian petrochemical refinery hub meeting agrarian north fuel demand.

places.name: Numaligarh
places.fact: Established under the historic 1985 Assam Accord, nicknamed the 'Accord Refinery'.

places.name: Bongaigaon
places.fact: Integrated refinery and petrochemical complex in lower Assam.

places.name: Tatipaka
places.fact: Mini refinery operated by ONGC processing local Krishna-Godavari condensate.

questions.question: Why is the location of the Mathura refinery considered ecologically sensitive?
wrong: Location on an earthquake fault line
questions.explanation: Mathura refinery emissions (SO2) created acid rain concerns regarding marble cancer at the Taj Mahal.

questions.question: Which refinery was established as a direct outcome of the 1985 Assam Accord?
questions.explanation: Numaligarh Refinery was set up in accordance with Commitments made in the Assam Accord of 1985.

questions.question: Which coastal facility houses the world's largest petroleum refining complex?
questions.explanation: Reliance Industries' Jamnagar complex possesses an aggregate capacity exceeding 1.24 million bpd.

title: Iron & Steel Plants
blurb: Integrated public and private steel manufacturing hubs and alloy centers.

places.name: Jamshedpur (TISCO)
places.fact: India's first private integrated steel plant founded by Jamsetji Tata in 1907 at Sakchi.

places.name: Bhilai
places.fact: Flagship SAIL plant built with Soviet collaboration; prime producer of railway rails.

places.name: Rourkela
places.fact: First public sector integrated steel plant built with German (Krupp-Demag) assistance; uses LD converter.

places.name: Durgapur
places.fact: SAIL plant built with British collaboration on the Damodar river bank.

places.name: Bokaro
places.fact: Built with Soviet assistance in 1964; uses coal from Jharia and iron ore from Kiriburu.

places.name: Visakhapatnam (RINL)
places.fact: India's only shore-based integrated public sector steel plant, having a natural deep harbor.

places.name: Salem Steel Plant
places.fact: Specialized SAIL facility producing world-class stainless steel utilizing local Kanjamalai iron ore.

places.name: Bhadravati (VISL)
places.fact: Founded by Sir M. Visvesvaraya as Mysore Iron Works in 1923; uses charcoal initially due to lack of coal.

places.name: Burnpur (IISCO)
places.fact: One of India's oldest integrated steel facilities, located on the Damodar river near Asansol.

places.name: Vijayanagar (JSW)
places.fact: JSW Steel flagship plant at Toranagallu utilizing rich Bellary-Hospet hematite ore.

places.name: Hazira
places.fact: AM/NS India coastal steel plant using direct reduced iron (DRI) on the Gulf of Khambhat.

places.name: Angul
places.fact: Jindal Steel and Power mega complex with India's first coal gasification-based DRI plant.

places.name: Kalinganagar
places.fact: Rapidly expanding modern steel cluster of Tata Steel in Jajpur district near Daitari mines.

questions.question: Which foreign nation provided technical assistance for the establishment of Rourkela Steel Plant?
questions.explanation: Rourkela Steel Plant was built in 1959 in collaboration with German firms Krupp and Demag.

questions.question: Which is the only shore-based integrated steel plant in India?
questions.explanation: Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited (RINL) in Visakhapatnam is India's only shore-based integrated steel plant.

questions.question: Why did the Bhadravati steel plant initially utilize charcoal rather than coking coal?
questions.correct: Absence of proximate coalfields in South India
wrong: Local iron ore required lower heat
questions.explanation: South India lacks Gondwana coking coal; Sir M. Visvesvaraya utilized charcoal from local Bababudan forests.

title: Mineral Belts & Mines
blurb: Strategic deposits of iron ore, copper, bauxite, uranium, gold and rare earths.

places.name: Kudremukh
places.fact: Horse-face shaped peak with high-grade magnetite; mining ceased due to ecological impact on Western Ghats.

places.name: Bailadila
places.fact: World-class high-grade hematite deposits (bullock hump shaped hills), exported to Japan via Vizag port.

places.name: Noamundi
places.fact: Premier hematite iron ore mine in West Singhbhum feeding Tata Steel since 1925.

places.name: Panchpatmali
places.fact: Largest bauxite deposit in Asia located in Koraput district, mined by NALCO for Damanjodi.

places.name: Lohardaga
places.fact: Historic bauxite mining hub of the Chota Nagpur plateau feeding Hindalco at Renukoot.

places.name: Khetri
places.fact: Hindustan Copper Limited (HCL) belt in the Aravallis mined since Harappan times.

places.name: Malanjkhand
places.fact: Largest copper ore open-pit mine in India, located in Balaghat district.

places.name: Koderma
places.fact: Historic 'Mica Capital of the World', known for premium ruby mica (muscovite).

places.name: Hutti
places.fact: Only operating active primary gold mine in India today, located in Raichur district.

places.name: Kolar Gold Fields (KGF)
places.fact: One of world's deepest historic gold mines in champion lode, ceased operations in 2001.

places.name: Zawar
places.fact: Ancient zinc smelting site (carbon-14 dated to 12th century AD) operated by Hindustan Zinc.

places.name: Jaduguda
places.fact: First uranium mine of India opened in 1967 in Singhbhum thrust belt (UCIL).

places.name: Tummalapalle
places.fact: One of world's largest uranium reserves hosted in Vempalle dolomites of Cuddapah basin.

places.name: Chavara
places.fact: Coastal placer mineral deposit rich in ilmenite, rutile, zircon and monazite sands.

places.name: Balaghat
places.fact: Accounts for ~80% of India's manganese production (Bharweli underground mine).

places.name: Sukinda
places.fact: Houses 95% of India's chromite deposits in Jajpur district, crucial for stainless steel.

questions.question: Which mine in the Cuddapah basin of Andhra Pradesh is estimated to host one of the world's largest uranium deposits?
questions.explanation: Tummalapalle in YSR Kadapa district was confirmed by DAE to possess exceptionally large uranium reserves.

questions.question: What strategic mineral is primarily extracted from the coastal beach sands of Chavara and Manavalakurichi?
questions.explanation: Monazite beach placers contain thorium, the cornerstone of Stage 3 of India's Nuclear Energy Programme.

questions.question: Kudremukh iron ore deposit in Karnataka is famous for which grade of ore?
questions.explanation: Kudremukh contains massive low-grade magnetite deposits enriched through beneficiation and piped as slurry to Mangalore.

title: Major Ports of India
blurb: Central government major ports and newly approved deep-draft landlord ports.

places.name: Deendayal (Kandla)
places.fact: Tidal port built in the 1950s after loss of Karachi to Pakistan; operates a major SEZ.

places.name: Mumbai Port
places.fact: India's premier natural deepwater harbor, historically the gateway of Indian oceanic trade.

places.name: Jawaharlal Nehru Port (JNPT)
places.fact: First 100% landlord major port in India and the busiest container handling gateway.

places.name: Mormugao
places.fact: Natural harbor at the mouth of the Zuari river, premier port for iron ore exports.

places.name: New Mangalore
places.fact: All-weather deep-water port handling Kudremukh iron ore pellets and POL imports.

places.name: Cochin Port
places.fact: Natural port situated on Willingdon and Vallarpadam islands in the Vembanad lake.

places.name: V.O. Chidambaranar (Tuticorin)
places.fact: Artificial deep-sea port in Gulf of Mannar handling thermal coal and Sri Lanka feeder traffic.

places.name: Chennai Port
places.fact: Second-oldest major port of India (artificial harbor opened in 1881), major car export hub.

places.name: Kamarajar (Ennore)
places.fact: India's first corporate major port (publicly corporatized under Companies Act).

places.name: Visakhapatnam Port
places.fact: Landlocked natural harbor protected by the Dolphin's Nose hill, deepest inner harbor.

places.name: Paradip Port
places.fact: Deep-draft port at the mouth of the Mahanadi river handling bulk iron ore and coking coal.

places.name: Kolkata & Haldia
places.fact: Only riverine major port in India, located on the tidal Hooghly river with diamond harbor.

places.name: Vadhavan
places.fact: All-weather deep-draft mega greenfield port approved in Palghar district with 20m draft.

questions.question: Which is the only riverine major port in India?
questions.explanation: Kolkata Port is located 203 km inland on the tidal Hooghly river system.

questions.question: Why was Kandla Port (Deendayal Port) developed after 1947?
questions.correct: To compensate for the loss of Karachi port to Pakistan
wrong: To establish a naval submarine base
questions.explanation: Partition gave Karachi port to Pakistan, necessitating a western deep gateway to serve Punjab, Rajasthan and Gujarat.

questions.question: Which major port in India was corporatized first as a public company?
questions.explanation: Kamarajar Port (Ennore) was originally incorporated under the Companies Act, 1956.

title: Nuclear Power Sites
blurb: Operating commercial reactors, fast breeders, and proposed mega parks.

places.name: Tarapur
places.fact: India's first commercial nuclear power station (1969), utilizing Boiling Water Reactors (BWR).

places.name: Rawatbhata (RAPS)
places.fact: First pressurized heavy water reactor (PHWR) in India, built in collaboration with Canada.

places.name: Kudankulam
places.fact: India's highest capacity NPP, featuring Russian VVER-1000 pressurized water reactors.

places.name: Kalpakkam (MAPS & PFBR)
places.fact: Indigenously designed PHWR and the site of India's Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (500 MWe).

places.name: Kaiga
places.fact: Located amidst Western Ghats on Kali river; holds world record for 962 days of continuous operation.

places.name: Kakrapar
places.fact: Site of India's first indigenously designed 700 MWe commercial PHWR reactor (KAPP-3).

places.name: Narora
places.fact: Located on the banks of Ganga in Uttar Pradesh; engineered for Seismic Zone IV.

places.name: Gorakhpur (GHAVP)
places.fact: First nuclear power plant in Haryana (Fatehabad district), utilizing water from Bhakra canal.

places.name: Jaitapur
places.fact: Proposed 9900 MWe mega nuclear park with French EPR reactors in Ratnagiri district.

places.name: Kovvada
places.fact: Proposed AP1000 pressurized water reactor complex in Srikakulam district (US collaboration).

places.name: Chutka
places.fact: Proposed 2x700 MWe indigenous PHWR project in Mandla district on the Narmada river.

places.name: Mahi Banswara
places.fact: Approved fleet-mode indigenous 4x700 MWe PHWR nuclear project in southern Rajasthan.

questions.question: Which nuclear reactor in India set a global record for continuous uninterrupted operation of 962 days?
questions.explanation: Kaiga Unit-1 operated continuously for 962 days before being safely shut down for planned maintenance.

questions.question: Which type of reactor is installed at the Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant?
questions.explanation: Kudankulam features Russian-supplied VVER-1000 light water reactors cooled and moderated by light water.

questions.question: Where is India's 500 MWe Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR) located?
questions.explanation: The PFBR is situated at the Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR) complex at Kalpakkam.

title: Dams & Barrages
syllabus: GS1 · Geography · Water Resources & River Systems
blurb: Architectural marvels across India's peninsular and Himalayan river systems.

places.name: Tehri Dam
places.fact: Highest dam in India (260.5 m) rock-and-earth fill embankment on Bhagirathi river.

places.name: Bhakra Dam
places.fact: Iconic concrete gravity dam on the Satluj river forming the Gobind Sagar reservoir.

places.name: Sardar Sarovar Dam
places.fact: Terminal concrete gravity dam on Narmada river supporting the Statue of Unity downstream.

places.name: Hirakud Dam
places.fact: Longest earthen dam in the world (25.8 km total length) built across Mahanadi river.

places.name: Nagarjuna Sagar
places.fact: World's largest masonry dam built across Krishna river between Nalgonda and Guntur.

places.name: Idukki Dam
places.fact: Concrete double-curvature parabolic thin arch dam between Kuravan and Kurathi hills on Periyar.

places.name: Koyna Dam
places.fact: Rubble-concrete dam on Koyna river, notorious for the 1967 reservoir-triggered earthquake.

places.name: Farakka Barrage
places.fact: Barrage diverting 40,000 cusecs of Ganga water into the Bhagirathi-Hooghly to flush Kolkata port.

places.name: Pong Dam
places.fact: Highest earth-fill dam in India on the Beas river forming Maharana Pratap Sagar Ramsar site.

places.name: Mullaperiyar Dam
places.fact: Masonry gravity dam located in Kerala on Periyar river but leased and operated by Tamil Nadu.

places.name: Almatti Dam
places.fact: Main reservoir of the Upper Krishna Project generating hydroelectric power in Bijapur district.

places.name: Gandhi Sagar
places.fact: First of the four major dams built on the Chambal river under the Chambal Valley Project.

places.name: Indira Sagar
places.fact: Key mother dam on Narmada river with the largest reservoir capacity in India (12.22 billion m3).

questions.question: The Idukki Dam in Kerala across the Periyar river is notable for which structural design?
questions.explanation: Idukki is one of the highest arch dams in Asia, constructed between two granite hills without spillways.

questions.question: Why was the Farakka Barrage constructed across the Ganga river in West Bengal?
questions.correct: To preserve and flush the Port of Kolkata from siltation
wrong: To irrigate dry districts of Purulia
questions.explanation: Farakka Barrage diverts water into the Bhagirathi-Hooghly system to maintain draft at Kolkata port.

questions.question: Which dam holds the title of the longest earthen dam in the world?
questions.explanation: Hirakud Dam across the Mahanadi has an overall dyke length extending over 25.8 km.

title: National Parks & Tiger Reserves
blurb: Prime habitats of the Royal Bengal Tiger, Asiatic Lion, and endemic fauna.

places.name: Jim Corbett
places.fact: India's first national park (1936, Hailey NP) and birthplace of Project Tiger in 1973 on Ramganga river.

places.name: Kaziranga
places.fact: UNESCO World Heritage site harboring two-thirds of world's great one-horned rhinoceros.

places.name: Keoladeo Ghana
places.fact: UNESCO site and Ramsar wetland famous for wintering Siberian cranes; Montreux Record site.

places.name: Ranthambore
places.fact: Junction of Aravalli and Vindhya ranges with historic 10th century fort inside.

places.name: Sundarbans
places.fact: World's largest mangrove delta, habitat of swimming tigers adapting to saline tides.

places.name: Gir National Park
places.fact: Only surviving natural sanctuary of the Asiatic Lion (Panthera leo persica) in Kathiawar peninsula.

places.name: Bandipur
places.fact: Part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, contiguous with Mudumalai, Wayanad and Nagarhole.

places.name: Periyar
places.fact: Cardamom hills sanctuary surrounding Periyar lake, notable for Asian elephants and tigers.

places.name: Kanha
places.fact: Revived the hard-ground swamp deer (Barasingha - Mascot Bhoorsingh) from brink of extinction.

places.name: Hemis
places.fact: India's largest national park (>4400 sq km), renowned high-altitude home of the elusive Snow Leopard.

places.name: Silent Valley
places.fact: Tropical evergreen rainforest in Kundali hills saved from hydel project; home to Lion-tailed Macaque.

places.name: Namdapha
places.fact: Only park with 4 big cats: Tiger, Leopard, Snow Leopard, and Clouded Leopard (Mishmi hills).

places.name: Desert National Park
places.fact: Thar desert ecosystem and critical breeding ground of the Critically Endangered Great Indian Bustard.

places.name: Simlipal
places.fact: Mayurbhanj biosphere reserve famous for unique melanistic (pseudo-melanistic black) tigers.

places.name: Nokrek
places.fact: Garo Hills core biosphere reserve protecting gene sanctuary for wild Citrus indica.

questions.question: Which Indian national park is the only place in the world harboring four pantherine big cat species?
questions.explanation: Namdapha in Arunachal Pradesh hosts Tiger, Leopard, Snow Leopard and Clouded Leopard across altitudinal zones.

questions.question: The 'Bhoorsingh the Barasingha' is the official mascot of which national park?
questions.explanation: Kanha was the first tiger reserve in India to officially introduce a mascot to raise conservation awareness.

questions.question: Which river flows through the heart of Jim Corbett National Park?
questions.explanation: The Ramganga river and its tributaries form the central catchment of Corbett.

title: Biosphere Reserves
blurb: UNESCO Man and the Biosphere (MAB) reserves and representative ecosystems.

places.name: Nilgiri
places.fact: First biosphere reserve designated in India (1986); tri-junction of TN, Kerala and Karnataka.

places.name: Nanda Devi
places.fact: Himalayan reserve encompassing Rishi Ganga gorge and Valley of Flowers National Park.

places.name: Gulf of Mannar
places.fact: Southeast Asia's first marine biosphere reserve, sanctuary for the vulnerable Dugong (sea cow).

places.name: Sundarbans
places.fact: Tidal mangrove ecosystem in the Ganges-Brahmaputra delta, tiger conservation zone.

places.name: Nokrek
places.fact: Core zone in Garo Hills preserving wild progenitor species of modern citrus fruits.

places.name: Pachmarhi
places.fact: Satpura Range ecosystem featuring deep ravines, Sal forests, and endemic Indian Giant Squirrel.

places.name: Simlipal
places.fact: Red silk cotton tree haven in Mayurbhanj, home to Santhal tribes and elephant corridors.

places.name: Achanakmar-Amarkantak
places.fact: Maikal hills junction of Vindhyas and Satpuras, watershed source of Narmada, Son and Johilla.

places.name: Great Nicobar
places.fact: Southernmost biosphere reserve, home to Shompen indigenous people and Nicobar Megapode.

places.name: Agasthyamala
places.fact: Western Ghats biome in Kerala and TN, traditional homeland of the Kani tribal community.

places.name: Khangchendzonga
places.fact: High-altitude Himalayan biome containing Zemu glacier and sacred Tibetan Buddhist sites.

places.name: Panna
places.fact: Vindhyan belt reserve on Ken river; successfully reintroduced tigers after local extirpation.

places.name: Cold Desert
places.fact: Trans-Himalayan cold desert including Pin Valley National Park and Kibber Wildlife Sanctuary.

places.name: Dehang-Dibang
places.fact: Eastern Himalayan reserve encompassing Siang and Dibang river valleys with Takin.

places.name: Great Rann of Kutch
places.fact: Largest biosphere reserve in India by area, famous for seasonal salt desert and Indian Wild Ass.

questions.question: Which was the first Biosphere Reserve to be designated in India under the UNESCO MAB framework?
questions.explanation: Nilgiri was established in 1986 and was the first in India to be inducted into the World Network of Biosphere Reserves in 2000.

questions.question: Which Indian biosphere reserve is home to the primitive hunter-gatherer Shompen tribe?
questions.explanation: The Shompen are an indigenous Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG) native to Great Nicobar Island.

questions.question: The Ken-Betwa river linking project intersects which tiger reserve and biosphere reserve?
questions.explanation: The Daudhan dam of Ken-Betwa link submerges portions of the core habitat of Panna Tiger Reserve.

title: Ramsar Wetlands
blurb: Wetlands of international importance under the Ramsar Convention.

places.name: Chilika Lake
places.fact: First Indian Ramsar site (1981); Asia's largest brackish lagoon hosting Irrawaddy dolphins.

places.name: Keoladeo Ghana
places.fact: Man-made wetland on Gambhir and Banganga rivers; Montreux Record site.

places.name: Loktak Lake
places.fact: Pumdi-rich freshwater lake; hosts world's only floating national park (Keibul Lamjao).

places.name: Wular Lake
places.fact: One of Asia's largest freshwater lakes formed by tectonic activity on the Jhelum river.

places.name: Sambhar Lake
places.fact: India's largest inland saline lake; key wintering area for tens of thousands of flamingos.

places.name: Vembanad-Kol
places.fact: Longest lake in India (96 km), fed by 10 rivers; hosts the Nehru Trophy Snake Boat Race.

places.name: Renuka Lake
places.fact: Smallest Ramsar wetland in India (area ~0.2 sq km) dedicated to Goddess Renuka.

places.name: Tsomoriri
places.fact: Brackish trans-Himalayan lake at 4595m altitude, breeding ground of Black-necked Crane.

places.name: Bhoj Wetland
places.fact: Consists of Upper Lake (Bada Talab constructed by Raja Bhoj) and Lower Lake.

places.name: Deepor Beel
places.fact: Perennial freshwater lake and former channel of the Brahmaputra near Guwahati.

places.name: Kolleru Lake
places.fact: Located between Krishna and Godavari deltas; fed by Tammileru and Budameru streams.

places.name: Point Calimere
places.fact: Coastal tip of Cauvery delta with saline swamps, mangroves, and flamingos.

places.name: Harike Wetland
places.fact: Deep freshwater wetland created at the confluence of the Beas and Satluj rivers (Indira Gandhi Canal origin).

places.name: Bhitarkanika Mangroves
places.fact: Second largest mangrove ecosystem in India; prime breeding ground of Saltwater Crocodiles and Olive Ridley turtles.

questions.question: Which two Indian Ramsar wetlands are currently listed on the Montreux Record?
questions.explanation: The Montreux Record highlights wetlands where ecological character changes have occurred or are likely. Chilika was removed from the list after successful restoration.

questions.question: The Indira Gandhi Canal (Rajasthan Canal) originates from which Ramsar wetland?
questions.explanation: The canal originates from the Harike Barrage at the confluence of the Satluj and Beas rivers in Punjab.

questions.question: The unique floating heterogeneous biomass known as 'Phumdis' is characteristic of which wetland?
questions.explanation: Phumdis are floating masses of soil, vegetation and organic matter exclusive to Loktak Lake in Manipur.

title: UNESCO World Heritage Sites
blurb: Monuments, architectural masterpieces, and pristine natural biomes.

places.name: Ajanta Caves
places.fact: 29 rock-cut Buddhist cave monuments in Waghora gorge renowned for mural paintings.

places.name: Ellora Caves
places.fact: Monumental rock-cut temples (Buddhist, Hindu, Jain) featuring the monolithic Kailasa temple (Cave 16).

places.name: Taj Mahal

places.name: Hampi

places.name: Fatehpur Sikri

questions.question: What engineering ingenuity distinguishes the construction of the Ramappa Temple in Telangana?
questions.correct: Sandbox foundation and floating lightweight bricks

questions.question: The megalithic stone chariot at Vijaya Vittala temple is an iconic symbol of which UNESCO site?
questions.explanation: The stone chariot at Hampi is dedicated to Garuda within the Vittala temple complex.

blurb: Crater, tectonic, glacial, and coastal water bodies across physiographic zones.

places.name: Wular Lake
places.fact: Largest freshwater lake in India formed by tectonic activity on the Jhelum river basin.

places.name: Dal Lake

places.name: Pangong Tso
places.fact: World's highest saltwater lake (4350m); endorheic lake extending from Ladakh into Tibet.

places.name: Sambhar Lake

places.name: Tso Kar

places.name: Vembanad Lake

places.name: Sasthamkotta Lake

places.name: Hussain Sagar

places.name: Jaisamand Lake (Dhebar)

places.name: Chandra Taal

questions.question: Which unique geological lake in India was created by a meteorite collision in basaltic bedrock?
questions.explanation: Lonar in Buldhana district of Maharashtra is the world's only known hyper-velocity impact crater in basaltic rock.

questions.question: The Thanneermukkom Bund was constructed in which major water body to regulate saltwater intrusion?
questions.explanation: The Thanneermukkom salt water barrier divides Vembanad into a freshwater southern half and brackish northern half.

questions.question: Which barrier island separates the Pulicat brackish lagoon from the Bay of Bengal?
questions.explanation: Sriharikota barrier island shelters Pulicat lake and houses ISRO's Satish Dhawan Space Centre.

places.name: Shipki La

places.name: Lipulekh Pass

places.name: Mana Pass

places.name: Niti Pass

places.name: Nathu La
places.fact: Historic Silk Road pass connecting Sikkim with Tibet's Chumbi Valley, reopened for trade in 2006.

places.name: Jelep La

places.name: Bomdi La

places.name: Diphu Pass

places.name: Bhor Ghat

places.name: Thal Ghat (Kasara)

places.name: Palakkad Gap
places.fact: Major 30-km natural tectonic break in the Western Ghats between Nilgiri Hills and Anaimalai Hills.

questions.question: Through which Himalayan mountain pass does the Satluj River enter Indian territory from Tibet?
questions.explanation: The Satluj cuts through the Zaskar range and enters Kinnaur district of Himachal Pradesh at Shipki La.

questions.question: Which mountain pass links the Kashmir Valley with the Jammu plains through the Pir Panjal range?
questions.explanation: Banihal Pass connects Jammu with Srinagar; the historic Jawahar Tunnel and the new Banihal-Qazigund railway tunnel traverse it.

questions.question: The Palakkad Gap in the Western Ghats provides transport connectivity between which two regions?
questions.explanation: The Palakkad Gap is a low mountain pass linking Palakkad in Kerala with Coimbatore in Tamil Nadu.

places.fact: High peak of the Saltoro Range (7,742 m) towering over the Siachen Glacier area.

places.name: Anamudi

questions.question: Which peak is recognized as the highest point in the entire Peninsular South India?

questions.question: Guru Shikhar on Mount Abu marks the highest culmination of which mountain system?
questions.explanation: Guru Shikhar (1,722 m) is the highest elevation of the fold mountain Aravalli system.

places.name: Lothal
places.fact: Tidal dockyard port town on Bhogavo river with bead-making factory and terracotta sealings.

places.name: Kalibangan
places.fact: Site on dried Ghaggar river showing earliest ploughed agricultural field and fire altars.

places.name: Rakhigarhi
places.fact: Largest Harappan metropolis in India (Dhrishadvati basin) with genetic ancient DNA excavations.

places.name: Banawali
places.fact: Exhibited radial street planning, terracotta model of a plough, and high proportion of barley.

places.name: Ropar (Rupnagar)

places.name: Alamgirpur
places.fact: Easternmost boundary site of the Indus Valley Civilization located on the Hindon river in Meerut.

places.name: Sarnath
places.fact: Site of Buddha's first sermon (Dharmachakrapravartana); home of Ashoka's Lion Capital (National Emblem).

places.name: Sanchi
places.fact: Great Stupa commissioned by Ashoka with carved toranas (gateways) depicting Jataka tales.

places.name: Dhauli
places.fact: Site of the bloody Kalinga War on the Daya river; rock edict surmounted by the forepart of an elephant.

places.name: Jaugada

places.name: Junagadh (Girnar)

questions.explanation: Until Maski was discovered in 1915, inscriptions only used the title 'Devanampriya Priyadarsi'; Maski explicitly named 'Devanampriya Asoka'.

questions.question: The presence of a sophisticated stepped tidal dockyard is the defining feature of which Harappan port city?
questions.explanation: Lothal in Gujarat features a massive burnt-brick tidal basin identified as a dockyard connected to the Gulf of Khambhat.

questions.question: The rock inscription at Junagadh is famous for recounting the historic construction and repair of which reservoir?
questions.explanation: Junagadh rock contains inscriptions of Ashoka, Saka ruler Rudradaman I, and Gupta emperor Skandagupta concerning the Sudarshana lake bund repairs.
